result.summary: The intersection provides essential pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and signalized control. However, the presence of a high-speed right-turn slip lane and a wide multi-lane roadway increases pedestrian exposure and conflict potential.

hazards.name: Right-turn slip lane
hazards.description: A dedicated right-turn lane allows vehicles to maintain higher speeds while turning, creating a conflict point with pedestrians crossing to the channelizing island.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic without a central refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Main crossing across the multi-lane road

interventions.title: Slip Lane Reconstruction
interventions.description: Tighten the corner radius or remove the slip lane to slow turning vehicles and improve pedestrian visibility and safety.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and continuous sidewalks, providing basic pedestrian infrastructure. However, the lack of dedicated pedestrian signals and the wide corner geometry may lead to higher vehicle turning speeds and crossing uncertainty.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: There are no visible pedestrian signal heads, requiring pedestrians to rely on vehicle traffic lights which may not provide adequate clearance time.

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry is relatively open, which can encourage vehicles to make right turns at higher speeds through the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner adjacent to the white building

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve predictability and safety for people crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and reduce vehicle turning speeds at the intersection.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, curb ramps, and a marked zebra crosswalk. However, the lack of visible traffic control and the presence of parked vehicles near the corner create potential visibility hazards for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corner block the line of sight between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the intersection near the crosswalk

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Intersection
hazards.description: There are no visible stop signs or traffic signals to regulate vehicle flow at this crossing, increasing the risk of failure to yield.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Enhanced Signage
interventions.description: Install pedestrian crossing warning signs to alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure at a wide intersection adjacent to a high-speed roadway. While a sidewalk is present, it shows signs of poor maintenance and lacks connection to marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or pedestrian signals.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross a wide, multi-lane roadway without any marked crosswalk or signalization to guide them or alert drivers.

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: The sidewalk has vegetation growing through cracks and uneven surfaces, which can be a tripping hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian paths and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: ADA Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at all crossing points to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting specifically oriented toward the sidewalk and crossing areas to improve nighttime visibility.
